posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: Nope.  It's not limited how many card plays it can stop as long as it remains in play.  The destroy got interrupted by the Ennead actions from a card entering their trash.   So once the Ennead actions finish Buffer Overflow will be destroyed causing Parse to draw a card and the Ennead to finally play a villain card.
posts.raw: Nope.  It's not limited how many card plays it can stop as long as it remains in play.  The destroy got interrupted by the Ennead actions from a card entering their trash.   So once the Ennead actions finish Buffer Overflow will be destroyed causing Parse to draw a card and the Ennead to finally play a villain card.

posts.name: Roger the Alien

posts.name: WarrenAC
posts.cooked:
Yeah,  the Ennead are tricky - things that discard villain cards to the trash are dangerous to use because they will trigger them!  But I didn't realise that actually made Buffer Overflow stronger against challenge Ennead - since all the symbols are guaranteed to trigger,  you can at least suffer two less card play effects (if you are fighting those Ennead) since Buffer overflow can keep canceling cards until it gets destroyed - it does the discard first (and then discard effects resolve) and then it will do the destroy effect.  Technically it should attempt to destroy itself three times,  once for each discard,  but once it is destroyed the other attempts won't happen.

For non-challenge Ennead you usually want to try avoiding trashing cards to reduce the number of symbols being triggered. Cool interaction!

posts.name: Natediggadoggity
posts.cooked:
So, I’m not sure if this is a bug or not:
I’m fighting Apostate with ChronoRanger, and I put The Whole Gang on Apostate’s lowest hp relic. Apostate gets a couple more relics into play, but then I finally get him to low hp, and then do lethal damage. He destroys the relic with The Whole Gang, and then I can choose another target with 4 or less hp to destroy. I choose Apostate, and so he destroys another relic, but stays on his front side. Then, after all the effects are triggered, he flips, heals to 20hp, then immediately flips back to his front side, and it’s the next hero’s turn.

Is that correct behavior? And if it is, what happens if I have No Executions on his next lowest up relic?

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: The behavior sounds right.  He hadn't flipped when The Whole Gang triggered and since there was another Relics in play while he was being destroyed again he would destroy his lowest health relic.   If he didn't have any left then you would have beaten him.   If you had No Executions on the second one he destroyed I would expect he would flip.   The reason being that he still had a Relic he could attempt to destroy and the rest of the text for him flipping after that doesn't care if it went back into his deck.  I can try out this situation and see what happens but that is what I'd expect.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: ...Wow, that's a cool way to get rid of relics. o.o If you can deal with his flip side, of course.

posts.cooked:
Two potential bugs I ran into:

When huge Extremist Sky-Scraper uses her power to destroy a target when playing against challenge Chokepoint, after Sky-Scraper destroys the target Chokepiont steals it and Sky-Scraper deals each target 2 sonic damage instead of 1 target 3 damage.

If BoT Chrono-Ranger puts "Dead or Alive" OR "Kill on Sight" AND "The Whole Gang" on one of the ennead and uses his power on a second ennead target (I think it would also work with any other two non-hero targets but I havn't checked) upon one of them being destroyed, it will ask which bounty effect should activate first and you can chose to activate "Dead or Alive"/"Kill on Sight" first and draw the card(s), then activate "The Whole Gang" to destroy the second ennead (currently being targeted with BoT C-R's power) which then triggers a second round of "Dead or Alive" draw three cards and "The Whole Gang" destroy another target.  If you select the original ennead as the target to be destroyed, you can repeat the process on a loop infinitly drawing cards and "destroying" the targets back and forth until you choose to skip the bounty effects.
